label: REAL_PAYPAL_SANDBOX
what: Each action ran once through its real workflow, then the worst crash was simulated (PayPal accepted the call, PayFlow lost the reply: status rewound to SUBMITTING with an expired lease and no stored result). The normal recovery path (runAction) re-sent it with the same PayPal-Request-Id / sender_batch_id. PayPal was then asked how many objects exist.

refund.how: PayPal replayed its original response for the repeated PayPal-Request-Id.

payout.how: PayPal refused the repeated sender_batch_id (HTTP 400, 'Batch with given sender_batch_id already exists') and linked the existing batch; PayFlow fetched it, proved sender_batch_id, receiver and amount are its own, and adopted it.

bugFoundByThisCheck.before: The replay was recorded FAILED although the payout existed (no duplicate money: PayPal's sender_batch_id guard held).
bugFoundByThisCheck.fix: createPayout adopts the linked batch after verifying it; the record was then recovered through the same path and is SUCCEEDED with UM2QM3S7JCSDC. The audit chain keeps both the failure and the recovery.
